model_annotation: The graph illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^0$ to $10^3$, with labeled tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 0 to 65, with major gridlines at intervals of 5. Each method is represented by a distinct colored line with a unique marker style, as indicated in the legend. The "Base" method (black line with circles) starts at approximately 39.5% and shows a slight increase to about 44.0%. The "MEND" method (brown line with diamonds) begins at 44.5% and rises to 56.5%. The "FT" method (blue line with triangles) starts at 39.8% and increases to 47.5%. The "MEMIT" method (purple line with squares) starts at 43.8% and increases to 55.0%. The "ROME" method (green line with squares) shows the highest performance, starting at 51.5% and increasing to 65.5%. All methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
